title: Building an assessment
lede: How JABSOM actually does it: copy last year, then edit. Writing from scratch is the exception.

blocks.title: Start from last year's exam
blocks.text: With roughly nine years of item data on the system, most JABSOM assessments are created by **copying the previous year's exam and editing it**, not by building a new one. This is the default path. It preserves question order, categorization, scoring setup, and the institutional memory of what worked.
Copy or repost: they are different things

blocks.title: For a new academic year, duplicate — do not repost
blocks.text: A repost folds this year's results into last year's reports, which corrupts year-over-year comparison. Duplicating gives the new exam its own Exam ID and its own reporting.

items.d: Give it a name that carries the academic year so it is findable next time.
